proposed_title: AP Reports Shifting Trump Administration Statements on Iran Operation
description_medium: An Associated Press report published March 2, 2026, compared the administration’s statements on Iran before later U.S.-Israeli strikes with its claims about earlier strikes. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the operation was not a regime-change war, then added, “the regime sure did change.” The reporting identifies no allied government that changed plans because of the statements.
description_long: On March 2, 2026, the Associated Press published a comparison of Donald Trump’s and his administration’s statements on Iran. AP reported that after U.S. strikes the previous summer, Trump and officials repeatedly said Iran’s nuclear program had been obliterated and its ability to make a weapon set back for years. In the immediate runup to later strikes with Israel, Trump and administration members issued more urgent warnings about Iran’s nuclear ambitions. At a Pentagon briefing, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said, “This is not a so-called regime change war,” and then, “the regime sure did change.” Those statements support a description of shifting and conflicting public explanations of the operation. They do not establish that a particular ally changed a military or diplomatic plan, sought clarification, or incurred a coordination cost. The title should therefore describe the public statements without asserting a consequence the reporting does not document.
